subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files as a core `bootstrap-extra-files` contract, or keep extra bootstrap loading limited to recognized workspace filenames?
rationale: The source behavior is clear, but broadening bootstrap injection changes deterministic startup context and the trusted file-loading contract, which is a product and security-boundary decision.

options.title: Approve Bounded In-Workspace Hook Contract
options.body: Allow custom-basename files through the existing hook path after the linked PR or a replacement preserves workspace containment, size budgets, docs, and session filtering.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and close or redirect these requests to narrower first-class filename or workspace-convention proposals.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context API
options.body: Keep this issue open or supersede it with a larger context API design if raw configured files are not the desired permanent contract.

recommendation.title: Approve Bounded In-Workspace Hook Contract
recommendation.body: Allow custom-basename files through the existing hook path after the linked PR or a replacement preserves workspace containment, size budgets, docs, and session filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest available routing signal for the product/security decision around workspace bootstrap and boundary-safe reads.
